results.title: The Price of Victory: A Machine Learning Analysis of How Salary Dispersion Influences Team Success in Major League Baseball
results.content: Using data from 29 MLB teams over eight seasons (2012-2019), this study uses multiple models, such as Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), panel data regressions, and Random Forest machine learning, to investigate the degree – if any – that inequalities in a team's payroll impacts success, measured by winning percentage. Keywords: Salary dispersion, team performance, Major League Baseball (MLB), Gini coefficient, panel data analysis, Random Forest, SHAP values, labor economics, sports economics. Interestingly, this aligns with the idea that investing in a franchise does not necessarily translate to new wins for the team; it essentially equals out to what fans expect with recent performance — log total payroll (0.0092) and Gini salary dispersion (0.0201) are both not statistically significant — meaning that real investment within a roster are less reflective of anticipated success than bonuses and salaries earned for on-field performance during the season.
